Subject: RE: Request for additional trial credits — NextWave Labs (fraud review)

Marissa / team — I ran a preliminary abuse/fraud check on NextWave Labs (account id: nw_9876). Findings below and attached:

- Usage pattern: 3 high-volume bursts (2025-12-10, 2025-12-28, 2026-01-18) each consuming ~250k tokens within 24–36 hours. Between bursts the account is idle.
- IPs: bursts originate from 2 distinct IP ranges; one resolves to a cloud provider (likely CI-based runs), the other to a residential ISP — mixed signals.
- Account creation and identity: account created 2025-11-29; billing info absent. Procurement contact listed but no signed SOW or PO on file.
- Similar requests: we have a record of two prior trial top-up approvals for this account (2025-12-01 and 2025-12-30).

Conclusion: pattern is suspicious for automated bulk evaluation or possible credit-farming across ephemeral projects. Recommend we do NOT auto-grant the full 300k. Options:
  1) Offer a limited 50k top-up one-time with usage caps and require a direct payment method or PO for further credits.
  2) Pause the account pending KYC/procurement evidence (PO or signed MSA).
  3) If Sales wants to salvage the opportunity, require a short paid pilot (30 days) with a credit applied to the invoice.

I've attached an excerpt of the audit log and a session-replay screenshot archive for your review. If Logan can confirm there's no runtime exploit or bug, we can move with option 1 while collecting PO.

-Dev Patel
Security & Fraud Ops
dev_patel@redwood.com

Alex — thanks for your patience. We completed an internal review. To be transparent, we saw repeated large bursts of usage on your account and multiple prior top-ups in the last 60 days, which triggered a fraud/abuse review.

We're happy to continue supporting your evaluation, but we need to do it under tighter controls so the program is fair and sustainable for all customers. Options for NextWave:

1) We can approve a one-time 50,000 credit top-up with a 14-day expiry and a usage cap of 10k tokens/hour. This will be applied immediately if you confirm a valid PO or a payment method on file.

2) If you prefer more runway, we can set up a short paid pilot (estimated cost outline available) where we grant trial-like access but require a purchase order / card on file. The credit can be applied to the invoice.

If neither option works, we'll have to close the trial access and recommend you re-engage once procurement is ready. Please note we reserve the right to suspend accounts where evidence of systematic credit-farming is found.

Next steps: reply to confirm which option you'd like and attach a PO if selecting option 1. If you have questions about the audit excerpts I've attached, Evelyn on CS can walk through rate-limiting and best practices to get the benchmarks you need within the limited cap.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
